title: AI Bias, Privacy and Reliability
introduction: Responsible use begins by recognising where AI systems can cause harm or produce unreliable results.
learningOutcomes: Explain how dataset bias can affect outputs.
Describe the role of human oversight.

activities.question: A face-recognition system was evaluated mostly on one demographic group. What is the key concern?
options: Its performance may be worse for under-represented groups
It will automatically become artificial general intelligence
Its files will always be too small
activities.explanation: Unrepresentative data can hide unequal error rates and lead to poorer performance for groups with too few examples.

activities.question: Removing a person's name always makes a dataset completely anonymous.
activities.explanation: Other details can sometimes be combined to identify a person, so privacy needs broader assessment.

activities.question: Put these actions in a sensible order before relying on a high-impact AI output.

items.text: Have an accountable person review the result
Check the input and operating context
Compare the output with reliable evidence

activities.explanation: First understand the case, then verify the output against evidence, with an accountable human making or reviewing the decision.
